findings.statement: Reliance Retail is the largest and most profitable retailer in India, operating an integrated ecosystem with physical stores, digital commerce, and distribution platforms.

During FY 2025-26, Reliance Retail recorded Gross Revenue of ₹ 3,71,085 crore, representing a 12.1% growth over the previous year, with an EBITDA of ₹ 27,034 crore translating to an EBITDA margin of 8.2%.
For the consolidated entity in FY 2025-26, net profit before share of profit / (loss) of associates / joint ventures and tax was ₹ 1,23,162 crore, compared to ₹ 1,06,017 crore in FY 2024-25.
Consolidated Net Cash Flow from Operating Activities was ₹ 1,92,113 crore in FY 2025-26 compared to ₹ 1,78,703 crore in FY 2024-25.
The Net Profit Margin for the consolidated entity increased from 6.3% in FY 2024-25 to 8.0% in FY 2025-26 due to higher net profit.
Return on Capital Employed increased from 14.6% in FY 2024-25 to 20.7% in FY 2025-26, driven by higher profit and reduction in capital employed.
Total consolidated borrowings stood at ₹ 3,74,421 crore as of 31st March, 2026, up from ₹ 3,47,530 crore as of 1st April, 2025.
Carrying amounts of financial liabilities part of supplier finance arrangements stood at ₹ 76,377 crore consolidated as of 31st March, 2026.
Consolidated cash generated from operations was ₹ 2,01,721 crore in FY 2025-26, following working capital adjustments of ₹ 12,497 crore.
Consolidated closing cash and cash equivalents were ₹ 1,45,977 crore as of 31st March, 2026, up from ₹ 1,06,502 crore a year prior.
Management highlights an increase in the Debt Service Coverage Ratio to 4.03 in FY 2025-26 from 2.06 in FY 2024-25, attributed to lower finance costs and principal loan repayments.
RIL stated it will continue to explore sophisticated financing structures to support expansion across both emerging and established verticals.
Bull case elements include S&P raising RIL's rating to A- in December 2025 due to rising contributions from less cyclical, consumer-facing businesses, alongside robust cash flows.
Bear case factors include heightened volatility in financial markets amid tariff uncertainty, global geopolitics, FPI outflows, rising trade deficits, and pressures on the Rupee.

findings.statement: In FY 2026, TCS consolidated revenue reached ₹267,021 crore, breaking down by industry vertical as Banking, Financial Services and Insurance at 38.7%, Consumer Business at 15.9%, Communication, Media and Technology at 14.8%, Life Sciences and Healthcare at 10.4%, Manufacturing at 10.0%, and Others at 10.2%.

Geographically, consolidated revenue concentration for FY 2026 was led by North America at 48.6%, United Kingdom at 17.4%, Continental Europe at 15.4%, APAC at 8.3%, India at 5.9%, and others including Latin America and MEA.
For the year ended March 31, 2026, TCS reported consolidated revenue from operations of ₹267,021 crore, representing a 4.6% increase over FY 2025, while constant currency revenue declined by 2.4%.
Operating profit (EBIT before other income) for FY 2026 was ₹66,838 crore with an operating margin of 25.0%, representing a 70 basis point improvement over FY 2025.
Over the past five financial years, TCS recorded a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 10.2% in revenue, scaling from ₹191,754 crore in FY 2022 to ₹267,021 crore in FY 2026.
Earnings per share grew at a 10.3% CAGR over the past five fiscal years, reaching ₹145.99 in FY 2026 compared to ₹103.62 in FY 2022.

Contractual maturities of consolidated financial liabilities as at March 31, 2026 included trade payables of ₹14,808 crore due in the first year, lease liabilities totaling ₹13,218 crore, and other financial liabilities totaling ₹11,227 crore.

TCS demonstrated high cash conversion, with shareholder payouts and cash metrics reflecting robust operational cash generation, including standalone net cash flows generated from operating activities of ₹45,597 crore for the year ended March 31, 2026.

Management highlighted a 4.6% reported revenue growth rate for FY 2026, while the underlying constant currency growth rate was a decline of 2.4% due to macroeconomic uncertainty, geopolitical tensions, and the completion of a large domestic transformation program.
Certain non-recurring items such as restructuring charges, legal claim provisions, and Labour Code impacts were excluded from reported management commentary metrics to present underlying performance.
Management noted that the company does not provide any specific revenue or earnings guidance.
Total shareholder payouts for FY 2026 included three interim dividends of ₹11 each, a special dividend of ₹46, and a recommended final dividend of ₹31, summing to ₹110 per share.
The bull case highlights industry-leading return on equity, strong order books with significant multi-year TCV momentum, and growing leadership in AI-led enterprise transformation services.

The bear case points to macro uncertainty, customer discretionary spending scrutiny, litigation and regulatory exposures such as US$ 112 million provided for a legal claim, and potential pricing deflation from emerging deep-tech AI competitors.

findings.statement: Reliance operates an integrated retail ecosystem spanning physical stores, digital commerce, and distribution platforms, recording Gross Revenue of H 3,71,085 crore and EBITDA of H 27,034 crore in FY 2025-26.
The Oil to Chemicals (O2C) segment generated revenue of H 6,62,401 crore and EBITDA of H 60,546 crore for FY 2025-26, supported by transportation fuel cracks and efficient feedstock sourcing.
For the consolidated entity in FY 2025-26, Net Profit Before Share of Profit/(Loss) of Associates/Joint Ventures and Tax was H 1,23,162 crore, compared to H 1,06,017 crore in FY 2024-25.
Standalone Net Profit Before Tax for FY 2025-26 was H 54,076 crore, up from H 46,128 crore in FY 2024-25.
S&P raised RIL's rating from BBB+ to A- in December 2025 due to the rising contribution of less cyclical, consumer-facing businesses.
Consolidated borrowings as of March 31, 2026 stood at H 2,96,716 crore for non-current borrowings (including current maturities) and H 77,705 crore for current borrowings.
Consolidated financial liabilities part of supplier finance arrangements stood at H 76,377 crore as of March 31, 2026.
Net cash flow from consolidated operating activities for FY 2025-26 was H 1,92,113 crore, compared to H 1,78,703 crore in FY 2024-25.
Consolidated cash generated from operations reached H 2,01,721 crore in FY 2025-26 after net working capital adjustments of H 12,497 crore.

Management highlighted strong retail store performance and expansion, while reported segment financials noted that retail EBITDA margins experienced a slight moderation due to the growing contribution of hyper-local commerce.
Management expects retail online transition scale benefits to translate into value through FY 2028 and FY 2029.
Management noted that the FY 2026-27 O2C outlook remains extremely vulnerable to geopolitical, macroeconomic, and policy risks such as SAED and feedstock directives.
The bull case features strong omni-channel retail scale, robust consumer and digital subscriber growth, flexibility in refining operations, and an S&P credit rating upgrade to A-.
The bear case encompasses geopolitical volatility, regulatory and tax risks like SAED directives, downstream chemical overcapacity, and margin dilution from hyper-local commerce expansion.
